---
title: "x402 Paid API"
description: "Scaffold an API that agents can pay for, in stablecoins on Celo."
icon: "credit-card"
---

## What you get

```bash
npx @celo/celo-composer create my-app -t x402
```

An `apps/api` workspace containing both halves of an x402 payment:

- a **seller** — a Hono server whose `POST /paid` answers `402 Payment Required` with what it accepts
- a **buyer** — a script that reads those requirements, pays them, and prints the settlement hash

It points at Celo Sepolia by default, so the whole loop runs for free.

## How x402 works

An agent calls your endpoint. You answer `402` with a machine-readable description of
what you accept: asset, amount, recipient, network. The agent signs an EIP-3009
authorization for exactly that and calls again. A **facilitator** verifies the
signature, submits the transfer on chain, pays the gas, and only then does your
handler run.

The part developers do not expect: **the buyer needs no CELO.** The authorization is
signed off-chain and the facilitator sponsors the gas, so an agent holding nothing but
a stablecoin can transact.

Celo hosts a facilitator per network, so you do not run one:

| Network | Facilitator | CAIP-2 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Celo Sepolia (default) | `https://api.x402.sepolia.celo.org` | `eip155:11142220` |
| Celo mainnet | `https://api.x402.celo.org` | `eip155:42220` |

## Running it

```bash
cd apps/api
cp .env.template .env
```

Set `X402_PAY_TO` to an address you control — until it is set, `/paid` answers for
free — `X402_API_KEY` to a facilitator key from the Celo team, and
`BUYER_PRIVATE_KEY` to a throwaway key holding a little testnet USDC.

```bash
pnpm api:dev    # seller on http://localhost:3001
pnpm api:buy    # buyer pays it
```

The buyer prints the settlement transaction and an explorer link.

## Things that catch people out

**The price is in raw units.** USDC has 6 decimals, so `10000` is 0.01 USDC.

**The token must implement EIP-3009.** The `exact` scheme signs a
`transferWithAuthorization`. A token without it cannot settle through this path
regardless of what `asset` says. That is why the template uses USDC.

**`extra` is the EIP-712 domain and cannot be read from the contract.** If the `name`
or `version` is wrong the token rejects the signature at settlement, after everything
else looked correct.

**The facilitator API key is required, including on testnet, and its absence is
invisible until the last step.** `/supported` and `/verify` both answer without one,
so the server boots and returns a correct 402; only `/settle` returns 401, after the
buyer has signed. The generated seller warns about this at startup.

## What this template skips

No wallet provider and no smart contract framework are scaffolded. The seller needs
neither — it verifies signatures rather than holding a wallet — and the buyer reads a
key straight from the environment. `apps/web` is generated as the standard Celo
Composer frontend and is left untouched.
